value.kbd_note: Command-Shift-1 ejects; the Finder is the only shell, so key proof is a menu or a dialog, never a prompt
value.note: ABSOLUTE pointer: kh-ramabs writes MTemp/RawMouse in Mac OS low memory and publishes with CrsrNew := CrsrCouple, so the commanded pixel is the landed pixel and the guest's tracking curve is bypassed. No exec channel - System 7 has no shell at all.

labctl.notes: no exec channel: System 7.5.3 has no shell, no telnet and no serial console - the framebuffer is the only observation surface. The pointer is ABSOLUTE via `-device kh-ramabs` writing Mac OS's own low-memory globals; `labctl abs x y` lands on the commanded pixel. Drive a CLONE with scripts/install-vision/adb_pointer.py, never this dir.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# macos753 (slot 142) — the fleet's FIRST foreign-architecture QEMU station:
#   qemu-system-m68k -M q800 (Motorola 68040), Mac OS 7.5.3. Built from the
#   kernel-hive QEMU fork and installed to /opt/qemu-m68k, NOT from pve-qemu —
#   the fleet package ships no m68k target, and a checkpoint baked and loaded by
#   the same standalone binary never needs pve's pbs-state vmstate section.
#   TCG only (no KVM for m68k), so idle auto-pause carries its cost.
#   RELATIVE ADB pointer — no absolute path exists on this machine, and the
#   guest moves 0.36 px per delta unit, hence SH_CURSOR_SCALE=2.7778.
#   PRAM is a qcow2, not raw: a raw if=mtd drive makes savevm refuse outright.

launcherParity.reason: tracked verbatim launcher equals the live launcher; the golden was COLD re-baked 2026-08-23/24 with this exact guest-visible device set (including the q800's built-in dp83932 SONIC) on the standalone /opt/qemu-m68k build - snapshot `golden` in macos753-golden.qcow2 / pram-golden.qcow2, dated 2026-08-24 01:01:30, VM_CLOCK 0000:02:03.500 (note this machine keeps its vmstate in the PRAM qcow2, so the pair is what carries the checkpoint). NO GOLDEN RE-BAKE FOR THE ABSOLUTE POINTER, and this is the record of why so it is not re-derived: `-device kh-ramabs` is a BUS-LESS device with no VMStateDescription and no guest-visible hardware - it exposes no MMIO, no bus presence and no IRQ, and contributes no section to the migration stream - and the -chardev beside it is host-side wiring. The GUEST-VISIBLE device set is byte-for-byte the one the golden was baked against and `loadvm golden` still binds. INSTALL ORDER IS BINDING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: the QEMU binary must be in place BEFORE this launcher (`-device kh-ramabs` is an unknown device on the older binary and QEMU refuses to start outright), and the streamhost binary BEFORE the env fixture (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=ramabs panics an older daemon at startup). binarySha256 IS NOW SET (7bac9cce...), read from the installed /opt/qemu-m68k/bin/qemu-system-m68k after the 2026-08-31 cutover. The sentence that stood here said it was deliberately unset because no rebuilt binary had been installed -- true when written, made false by the cutover itself. A justification that has been overtaken argues against fixing the thing it describes, which is worse than no justification at all.

pointerRamAddress.derivedAgainstGolden: not derived against a golden - see durability
pointerRamAddress.note: Guest-physical address of MTemp, the first of classic Mac OS's pointer low-memory globals; the control object derives RawMouse (+0x04), Mouse (+0x08), CrsrPin (+0x0C), the current cursor's hotSpot (+0x5C), CrsrNew (+0xA6) and CrsrCouple (+0xA7) from it at fixed documented offsets. DURABILITY IS THE IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM rhapsody's pointerRamAddress, and the two must not be assumed alike because they share a field name and a method: rhapsody's address was FOUND BY SEARCHING ONE CHECKPOINT'S RAM and dies with a re-bake, so re-baking its golden means re-deriving it. This one is ARCHITECTURAL - low memory is at guest-physical 0 on q800 and Mac OS 7.5.3 leaves it identity-mapped, and these offsets are fixed by the OS (Inside Macintosh / SysEqu.a), not by any particular RAM image. A re-bake does NOT invalidate it, and nothing here needs re-deriving. WRITE SET IS LOAD-BEARING: MTemp and RawMouse are written; `Mouse` is NEVER written, because it is both the read-back sensor and the cursor VBL task's own change detector - writing it makes the task conclude nothing moved, so it clears CrsrNew and draws nothing while every global reads back correct. kh-ramabs verifies the address at connect by writing and publishing a position the guest is NOT at and requiring `Mouse` to arrive there, and refuses every write if that fails.

qemuBuild.note: Built from fork c5449c80 (merged 0007) with NO 0006 -- that patch is rhapsody's x86 i8259 fix and does not apply to m68k. binarySha256 read from the INSTALLED file at /opt/qemu-m68k/bin/qemu-system-m68k, not from a build log. Restore-proven on the live station: loadvm golden succeeded under this binary WITH -device kh-ramabs attached, running inode equal to the on-disk inode. Previous binary kept as <path>.pre-abs-bak (c2e90aae...), which does NOT know kh-ramabs -- the launcher arms the device unconditionally, so binary and launcher must be rolled back together or not at all.

reset.fixture: Quiet Mac OS 7.5.3 Finder desktop at 1152x870x8 (Apple 21-inch mode): Macintosh HD top-right, empty Trash bottom-right, no window open, nothing selected. Mouse tracking pinned to 'Very Slow', the only NON-accelerated setting Mac OS offers and therefore the only one under which 1:1 is reachable; double-click speed slowest so a click pair survives the stream. 32-bit addressing on (it defaults OFF, capping usable RAM at 8 MB of the 128) and disk cache raised from 32K to 7680K. loadvm restores in 0.32 s, framebuffer-identical to the baked scene.

museum.blurb: The Macintosh at its most familiar — grey desktop, one menu bar, a Trash in the corner — running on the 68040 Quadra that closed out the pre-PowerPC era.
museum.notes: The only station in the lineup emulating a 68000-family machine. Everything here is drawn by an OS with no protected memory and no command line at all.

network.note: retronet web plane: the q800's BUILT-IN dp83932 (SONIC) is a REAL bridged NIC on vmbr-rn via the persistent tap macosrn0 (streamhost/stations/macos753/rn-tapnet.sh, called `up` from the launcher on every start), MAC RN_MACOS753_MAC on the Apple OUI 08:00:07 which this guest forces. It is the ONLY NIC model -M q800 offers, and Mac OS 7.5.3 drives it with nothing installed - MacTCP lists Ethernet on the first cold boot. Addressed 10.99.0.23 with DNS 10.99.0.2 and Gateway Address 0.0.0.0, so NO default route - STATIC, not DHCP, because MacTCP 2.0.6 has no DHCP client at all (its choices are Manually / Server (BOOTP-RARP) / Dynamically), so the reservation exists only to keep the address unique. The config lives in the MacTCP Prep file in the System Folder, on the disk, and needs a guest restart to take effect. Behind the fail-closed MACOS753RN-IN guard chain it reaches ONLY the gateway CT 10.99.0.2, where Netscape Navigator 3.04 reads the corpus on :80 seamlessly (wildcard DNS, no proxy configured); never labhost, the LAN, the gallery or the internet. MacTCP is DORMANT until an app opens it, so the guest does not answer ping at the checkpoint - silence on the wire is the resting state, not a fault. Added 2026-08-23; the station previously had no NIC at all, so the golden was COLD re-baked (docs/lab/retronet/WEB-STATION-macos753.md)
